points.quote: `workbench.desktop.main.ts` imports `workbench.common.main.js` and then adds the desktop-only pieces: `electron-browser/desktop.main` and `desktop.contribution`, the native text file service...
`workbench.web.main.ts` (with `workbench.web.main.internal.ts`) imports the same common entry, then the web-specific services (`browser/web.main.ts`, `web.factory.ts`, `web.api.ts`).
`workbench.common.main.ts` imports everything that is common to both builds
Each platform provides its own implementation of a service interface. For example, the desktop build registers the native text file service. Callers depend only on the interface.
A feature is only loaded if some entry file imports it, usually through a `*.contribution.ts` file.
If a contribution isn't imported by `common`, `desktop` or `web`, it never ships.
